headlines.article_text: Figma (FIG) Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Figma exceeded consensus on third-quarter results and guidance. Net loss narrowed to $81.3 million from a loss of $1.10 billion a year ago. In this article FIG Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Figma signage appears at the New York Stock Exchange in New York as the company prepares for its shares to begin trading on July 31, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Figma shares tumbled 7% in extended trading after the company reported third-quarter results and guidance that surpassed Wall Street's predictions. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: 10 cents adjusted vs. 5 cents expected Revenue: $391.4 million vs. $375.8 million expected Figma's revenue grew about 43% year over year in the quarter, according to a statement . Net loss narrowed to $81.3 million, or 15 cents per share, compared with a loss of $1.10 billion, or $2.72 per share, a year earlier. The company's 12% adjusted operating margin exceeded the 6.1% consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. Executives lifted the full-year forecast. Figma now anticipates an 11% operating margin, up from 9% as of August, and $1.497 billion to $1.499 billion in revenue, compared with $1.463 billion to $1.467 billion before. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.471 billion in 2026 revenue. The company sees fourth-quarter revenue growth slowing to about 33%. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted 28% growth. Figma's announcement comes a day after highly valued design software startup Canva said it would cut 22% of its employees. Read more CNBC tech news Elon Musk's record election bet backfired. The backlash may reach beyond one billionaire Apple warns of risks related to AI agents behaving in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways AMD's data center revenue nearly doubles and Lisa Su expects growth to accelerate Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI Shares have come down about 41% so far in 2026, while the S&P 500 index has gained 12%. Earlier this year, investors became concerned that artificial intelligence models could pose a competitive risk to Figma. Across much of software, AI panic has largely subsided as incumbents have posted persistent growth. Figma wants to benefit from the rising adoption of AI to build websites and apps. During the quarter, the company started giving more AI credits to clients while maintaining prices. "What that means is you're potentially trading off near-term revenue, investing in your customers, and then allowing yourself to then grow durably over the long term," Figma's finance chief, Praveer Melwani, told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday. The number of weekly users working at organizations that spend over $10,000 on Figma who used AI credits increased by almost 50% during the quarter, Figma said in the statement. The share of work the company's own AI model performs doubled, and the rate of people undoing AI-generated work has fallen . "If there's certain actions that we can power for our customers at lower latency, lower cost, or similar quality to third party, we're open to that as well," Melwani said. Figma is increasing its focus on cybersecurity, said Dylan Field, Figma's co-founder and CEO. In recent months, AI agents have infiltrated systems at Hugging Face and other companies. Clients aren't asking Figma to become a security vendor, but the company must scrutinize "the security of all of our vendors right now," Field said. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Snap shares sank over 10% when the Snapchat parent missed on revenue and daily active users in its third-quarter earnings report Wednesday. Here's how the company did compared with analysts' expectations: Earnings per share : 3 cents. That figure is not comparable to analysts' estimates. Revenue : $1.72 billion vs. $1.73 billion expected, according to LSEG Global daily active users : 495 million vs. 499 million expected, according to StreetAccount Global average revenue per user, or ARPU : $3.48 vs. $3.48 expected, according to StreetAccount Sales in Snap's third quarter jumped 14% year-over-year while net income came in at $56 million, compared to the $104 million net loss it logged the prior year. Snap's third-quarter adjusted earnings came in at $383 million, topping the $337 million that analysts were projecting, according to StreetAccount. The Snapchat parent said fourth-quarter revenue should come in between $1.95 billion and $1.99 billion. The midpoint of that figure is higher than Wall Street's estimates of $1.95 billion. Fourth-quarter adjusted earnings are expected to come in between $490 million and $525 million. Analysts were expecting that figure to be $498 million. Snap executives said in an investor letter that the company plans for globally monthly active users to become its "primary audience metric" starting in its first quarter for 2027. The company also said it has 977 MAU for the quarter. "Daily engagement has historically been stable as a percentage of monthly engagement, but we do not intend to optimize Snapchat around daily use at the expense of long-term value for our community," the investor letter said. "A longer-term horizon better aligns our reported metrics with the product and safety decisions that strengthen relationships, create lasting utility, and support broader, more durable audience growth." Snap chief commercial officer Ronan Harris told analysts during an earnings call that lower spending by unspecified consumer packaged goods, or CPG, companies impacted third-quarter sales. Harris attributed the curbed CPG spending to "macro pressures in the U.S. and also the Middle East." "As we look ahead, we're seeing very positive signs of growth from diversified verticals like financial services in the U.S.," Harris said. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: COHR, APP, EXPE & more Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves after the bell: Qualcomm — The chipmaker fell almost 6% despite reporting a slight earnings beat in its fiscal fourth-quarter financial report . Further, Qualcomm sees adjusted earnings of $2.15 to $2.35 per share in the current quarter, while analysts sought $2.26 per share, per FactSet. AppLovin — The AI stock surged more than 20% after the software company known for mobile game advertising posted third-quarter results that topped estimates. AppLovin posted adjusted EBITDA of $1.84 billion, greater than the $1.73 billion consensus estimate, according to FactSet. Revenue of $2.18 billion exceeded the forecast $2.07 billion. Expedia — Shares tumbled more than 7% after it delivered mostly weaker-than-expected guidance for the current quarter. The online booking company forecasts revenue between $3.69 billion and $3.75 billion in the fourth quarter, but analysts polled by FactSet on average expected $3.74 billion. The company, however, beat estimates for both earnings and revenue in the third quarter. Coherent — The optical materials company gained 7% after reporting adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share, compared to analysts polled by FactSet's estimates for $1.99 per share. Revenue also came in above estimates, as did guidance for the current quarter. Zillow — Shares sank more than 16% after the company missed on key metrics in its third-quarter earnings report. Adjusted earnings came in at 55 cents per share, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's estimates for 59 cents. Revenue also was weaker than expected, at $724 million compared to expectations for $754 million. Klaviyo – The maker of the customer relationship management platform slid about 5% even as the company reported third-quarter results that beat estimates. Klaviyo posted adjusted earnings of 22 cents per share on revenue of $387.2 million. The FactSet consensus called for 17 cents per share and $380 million. Klaviyo also lifted its full-year revenue guidance. MercadoLibre – The e-commerce platform slid about 7% after third-quarter earnings missed expectations. MercadoLibre earned $8.83 per share, compared to the FactSet consensus estimate of $9.27 a share. Revenue of $10.75 billion beat the estimate for $10.69 billion, however. Arm Holdings — Shares dipped almost 2% despite the designer of central processing units delivering a strong earnings report. The UK-based company reported adjusted earnings of 52 cents per share, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's consensus estimates for 47 cents Cava — Shares fell more than 11% after it reported third-quarter 2026 financial results , missing Wall Street expectations. Earnings came in at 11 cents a share, versus the LSEG consensus estimate for 12 cents. Cava posted revenue of $356 million, while analysts expected the number to be $359 million. Wolfspeed – The semiconductor manufacturer dropped 5% after posting a wider-than-expected loss in the fiscal first quarter. Wolfspeed's adjusted loss of $2.03 per share came in worse than the FactSet consensus estimate for a $1.99 per share loss. Figma — The software stock dropped almost 7% even after the cloud-based design platform posted third-quarter results that blew away expectations. Figma posted adjusted earnings of 10 cents a share on revenue of $391 million, while the LSEG consensus called for 5 cents a share and $376 million. HubSpot – Shares fell more than 8% after the company's fourth-quarter earnings and revenue guidance came up short of expectations. HubSpot expects to earn between $3.85 and $3.87 per share on revenue of $945 million to $947 million. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $4.09 in earnings per share and $964.9 million in revenue. However, the company's third-quarter earnings and revenue beat expectations. e.l.f. Beauty – Shares of the cosmetics company gained more than 4%. Fiscal second quarter results surpassed estimates, with e.l.f. posting adjusted earnings of $1.21 per share and revenue of $521 million. Analysts polled by LSEG sought 60 cents per share and $470 million. Snap – Shares of the social media company tumbled 7%. Third-quarter revenue of $1.72 billion narrowly missed the LSEG consensus estimate of $1.73 billion. Global daily active users also fell short of expectations, coming in at 495 million versus the StreetAccount consensus of 499 million. Dutch Bros — The coffee chain sank 19% after it cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $380 million from a previous range of $385 million to $390 million. Same-store sales in the third quarter also came in weaker than expected at 4.4%, versus the StreetAccount consensus estimate of 4.6%. Fastly – The edge cloud platform saw shares plummet 16%, even as earnings and revenue in the third quarter topped estimates, as did guidance for the current quarter. The company announced Scott Lovett, president of Go To Market, will be retiring in 2027. — CNBC's Sarah Min, Sean Conlon, Ananya Chetia and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting
